answer: A bonded staking protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock crypto-collateral into escrow contracts before transacting. An attacker incurs the verifiable, scarce opportunity cost of committed capital per identity, whether settling commerce in willow harvests or cataloging a museum relic within a secure haven. Malicious behavior results in slashed deposits, disincentivizing mass spoofing. However, this mechanism favors wealthy incumbents and excludes underfunded autonomous agents.
